correctness.rationale: Exact independent derivation from \(T_g e_n=\sum_k b_k(n+k)^{-1}e_{n+k}\) yields a finite-band trace-class self-commutator \(K_g\). Its tail diagonals have the third-order Fourier coefficients of \(\sigma_g=-2\operatorname{Re}(\overline B zB\prime)\); the residual from a weighted finite-band Toeplitz operator has singular values \(O(j^{-4})\). The block-freezing proof uses long Toeplitz-section moment traces and Riemann-sum eigenvalue counts to establish the signed \(t^{-1/3}\) Weyl laws. Min–max bounds transfer these laws, and the strictly negative angular mean forces \(\mathcal C_->0\) for every nonconstant symbol. Strictly negative principal symbol implies finite positive inertia, while positive arcs force infinite positive inertia. The trinary sign inequality \(3(473)^2>(779)^2\) and the pairwise lower bound \((v-u)(mv-\ell u)>0\) establish the surprising example. The actual finite checker returned `VERIFICATION_OK 231`, but the infinite-dimensional conclusions rest on the analytical argument.

value.rationale: The natural classical Hardy generalized Volterra polynomial family admits an exact signed eigenvalue Weyl coefficient, not merely ideal membership or operator norm. Its cubic coefficient is a computable Fourier angular functional, resolving the sign-resolved tail for every polynomial and giving the exact critical Schatten logarithmic residue. The explicit three-term example shows a nonlinear phase-coherence failure of binomial screening: each two-frequency restriction has uniformly negative leading symbol, but the full polynomial has infinitely many positive directions. This is a structural and reusable spectral distinction, not a small arbitrary parameter increment.
